Details

Sample: every M3 recipe track (χ² < 1, 4 clusters, one ray per event) crossing det3’s interior, golden row sat_det3 (mx17_det3_saturday_scan_6-27-26 / long_run_resist_490V_drift_1000V), production table …/mx17_3/wft/final_phys/events.parquet (phys bundle, PIVOT_START). The budget is rerun/effbudget; the far classes are C22’s classifier (rerun/outliers/classify.py); the re-categorisation is summarize.recat().

"Recoverable" counts only what a reference-free change was shown to recover on these very events (re-running the production reconstruction with the change, then scoring against M3): band veto 0.79; spark veto 0.16; head-on rule 0.26. The multi-particle share (2.3 points: the M3 track is among det3’s reconstructed tracks) is a matter of the efficiency definition, not of the reconstruction.

Reproduce: rerun/satstudy/ README, run order. Outputs in ~/x17/cosmic_bench/satstudy/.

Details

summarize.recat(): first match wins, in the order detected, band, multi-particle, spark, the C22 far classes, head-on. band: the event carries a noise band (bands.py: ≥ 8 strips of a chip offset by > 5σ and flat) and production lost it to the n_dropped cut or the 50-hit spark veto, and sparks.py does not call it a discharge. multi-particle: multitrack.py class M, ≥ 2 particle-like candidate clusters in a view (time extent ≤ 24 samples); the old “found, cut” second-particle events are “M3 one fitted, cut”. The spark row lost the bands it used to contain: 26 of the 49 “muon + other” remain.

4

Details

bands.py. A channel is offset in a trigger when its common-mode-subtracted window mean is > 5σ of its pedestal noise while its RMS about that mean stays < 2σ: shifted, not pulsing. A band = ≥ 8 such channels in one 64-channel chip. Left / middle: the pedestal-subtracted window mean of each channel minus the chip median, before common mode, for random band triggers (colour) and three ordinary triggers (black). The offset sits on a contiguous run of channels (x: 32–63, y: 0–25 of the chip), up to the ADC rails; the block-median common mode removes most of it, which is why the displays show only ~100–300 ADC (median offset after CM 119 / 78 ADC x / y, 99 % 1516). Both signs, equally (53 % positive in x).

Table: rate of triggers with a band per view, all bench chambers (golden row: every trigger; others: the first 3 000 per file) and how often y has one when x does. On det3 the x band lives on strips x < 50 mm and the y band on y > 250 mm: one corner of the chamber, seen by both strip layers.

The chambers are gone, so the mechanism stays a stated limitation; the data fix below does not depend on it.

5

Details

bands.py report → bands.json (nulls, decay). SCA cell: (DREAM timestamp // 6) mod 512, 32 bins. Period: largest Rayleigh R of the band-trigger timestamps over 4 401 periods 10–32 ms (tick = 10 ns: the run spans 8 442 s in the HV log, 844·10⁹ ticks); “noise” is the expected maximum for random phases. Discharge: > 150 strips above 6σ (x + y). HV: hv_monitor.csv of the run, every imon channel. In-window discharges: ≥ 8 strips of a chip above 3000 ADC — they are spread over all chips while the bands sit on x chip 0 and y chips 5–7. Decay: per band channel with |offset| > 300 ADC, the least-squares slope of its waveform over the window divided by the offset; an exponential tail of time constant τ gives −1/τ. Common mode: fitting each channel’s residual against its chip’s common mode (all triggers) removes nothing — the offset is on a sub-range of the chip and independent of the chip’s own shift.

6

Details

Cost (bands.py report): 249 of 6,451 interior rays have a band in the trigger; 57.0 % of them are detected against 92.6 % without. Where they go: detected 57.0 %, rejected_cut 26.9 %, spark 11.2 %, far 4.8 %. The band strips form a competing cluster (n_dropped > 2) or push the event over the 50-hit spark veto; the track itself is usually fine (far rate unchanged). Note the loss does not depend on where the track is: the cut and the veto are event-wide.

Fix (reco_variant.py --drop-flat): drop every hit with trunc_left AND trunc_right (above threshold at the first and the last sample of the window) before seeding, so it neither clusters nor counts toward the veto. That is 84 % of the hits on band strips and 0.71 % of all others (these are mostly saturated or discharge strips). Re-running production with it on all 252 interior band events: 145 → 196 detected; by production category recovered: {'detected': 143, 'far': 1, 'rejected_cut': 49, 'spark': 3}. controls: 400/400 detected with the veto (production 400), 1 view(s) moved.

7

Details

Denominator. 6 451 = every event whose M3 reference (χ² < 1, 4 clusters, one ray per event) crosses det3’s interior. It is not the number of triggers (8 479 recipe rays in all, interior or not; far more triggers fail the recipe). Each class is a share of these 6 451.

Classes (multitrack.py count): S = ≤ 1 particle-like cluster in each view (6138); M = ≥ 2 in either view (187); V = spark-vetoed (126): production drops the event before fitting, so there are no candidates to count — it is lost under every rule. Particle-like = the cluster’s summed signal (strips within max(4, |15 tan θ| + 3) mm of its mid-gap position) stays above 20 % of its peak for ≤ 24 samples × 60 ns; a 30 mm column at 36 µm/ns is 14 samples plus the ~6-sample pulse. Longer clusters are the noise bands (slides “bands”) and are excluded. A particle-like cluster is not yet a verified through-going track: a compact δ blob or a short stub also qualifies; what the second particles are (shower partner, knock-on, independent muon) is open.

Sub-classes (multitrack.py sub, by production’s outcome): M3 particle fitted, then cut (69) — production’s winner was the M3 track but n_dropped > 2 rejected the view: the old “found, cut” second particle. Other particle picked (81) — the brighter other track won the largest-cluster ranking (charge ratio median 1.7), the M3 one is among the candidates: old “far”. Merged in one view (37) — no candidate near M3 in one view; 30 of them are 1×2 / 2×1, the two tracks overlap in one projection within the 12 mm seed gap; the joint two-track fit (WFT_TWO_TRACK_FIT) recovers 8 of them (next slide but one).

Rules. Production = the efficiency budget’s “detected”: the winning fit within 5 mm of M3 at the mesh (raw strip frame) in both views and n_dropped ≤ 2 — so 0 multi-particle events by construction (a particle-like second cluster has ≥ 3 strips). Any-candidate credit = some x and some y candidate within 5 mm, no pairing, no n_dropped cut (Dylan: “if there are two tracks and we reconstruct both, we should get credit if one matches M3”).

Recomputed from rows: summarize.multi_flow() over multitrack_det3.parquet and multi_sub.parquet (summary.json key multi_flow).

Details

Old → new. The old budget’s “found, cut” (136, 2.1 %: production found the M3 track, n_dropped > 2 rejected it) splits into 69 with a second particle-like cluster (the “M3 particle fitted, then cut” sub-class) and 67 whose extra strips were a noise band only — all 67 pass when the band strips are not counted. The C22 far class MULTI (122, 1.9 %) splits into 111 multi-particle (76 other picked + 35 merged) and 11 single-particle events whose second deposit is not particle-like. 7 of the 19 far:EDGE are multi-particle too. 187 = 69 + 111 + 7.

Budget bar vs this count. The re-categorised budget (slide “budget”) shows 183 multi-particle events (2.84 %), not 187: it takes the first matching class, and 4 of the “M3 particle fitted, then cut” events also carry a noise band, so they sit in “band”.

The arithmetic. Production counts 5 882 / 6 451 = 91.2 %. Single-particle efficiency: production 95.8 %; the band veto (n_dropped without the band clusters’ strips) adds 67 → 96.9 %, the number to quote first; any-candidate credit adds 9 more single-particle events (a candidate within 5 mm in both views that production did not pick) → 97.1 %. Total with any-candidate credit everywhere: (5 958 + 150 + 0) / 6 451 = 94.7 % (multitrack.json total.any). With singles at the band-veto number instead: 94.5 %. The spark-vetoed 126 (2.0 %) are lost under every rule: production never fits them (slides “spark”).

Counts: summarize.multi_flow() (summary.json key multi_flow), recomputed from the parquet rows.

9

Details

multitrack.py sub. Quality: per view the particle candidate nearest M3 within 5 mm, robust σ of its residual at the mesh and of its ladder-scaled angle difference, and the fraction agreeing with M3 (|dθ| ≤ 5°, |res| ≤ 3 mm). The M3 particle in a two-particle event is fitted to the single-track resolution; the slightly lower agreement comes from the closest pairs, whose charge overlaps the window.

M3 picked (69): the old “found, cut” second particle — production chose correctly, the n_dropped cut threw the event away. Other picked (81): the other particle is brighter (charge ratio median 1.7) and the largest-cluster ranking prefers it; the M3 track is among the candidates. Both are detected with multi-track credit. M3 not found (37): 30 of them see one cluster in one view and two in the other — the two tracks overlap in that projection, within the 12 mm seed gap, and one fit lands on the other track or between them.

Can the joint two-track fit (wft/TWO_TRACK_FIT_2026-09-16.md; its cross-view corroboration lowers the split threshold exactly when the other view shows two tracks) split them?

  • joint two-track fit (production settings): M3 track found (both views, any candidate) in M3-not-found events 8/37 (production 0); other-picked 81/81; controls: 0 of 150 single tracks split, 0 views moved.

10

Details

pairing.py. The rule (wft.reco.xy_pair_cost’s form): of the two assignments take the one with the lower summed cost, cost = Σ min(z², 25) of the x−y differences lq = ln(q_x/q_y), u50, u90 (charge-arrival quantiles) and, for real events only, t0; medians and robust σ from clean single tracks (σ(lq) = 0.054: one track’s x and y charges agree to 5 %).

Toy: 5,882 clean single tracks, calibration on odd event ids, test on even; 399,866 random pairs, each track keeping its own x and y. It is the infinite-separation limit (no merging, no shared strips). The only failures are pairs whose charges agree to better than ~2σ(lq) — Landau fluctuations make that rare (12 % of pairs within 10 %). The depth profile is an independent handle (80 % alone) that rescues half of those. t0 is left out of the toy (every donor has its own trigger); on real events, where both tracks share one, t0 alone pairs 65 %.

Real: the 110 multi-particle events with exactly two particle clusters per view and the M3 track on one of each; right = the M3-matched x and y end up together. The toy and the real events agree (95.8 vs 96.4 %).

Overlay bench (overlay.py; the bench version of intra_bench): two clean single tracks of the same file and trigger phase, t0 within 30 ns, summed in the waveforms; production seeding and fit unchanged; truth = each donor’s own fit. Per separation bin (min of x, y): 0–6 mm: both found 0 %; 6–12 mm: both found 0 %; 12–18 mm: both found 22 %, paired right by charge 100 %, + profile 100 %, production gate 33 %; 18–24 mm: both found 98 %, paired right by charge 100 %, + profile 100 %, production gate 46 %; 24–40 mm: both found 100 %, paired right by charge 98 %, + profile 100 %, production gate 60 %; 40–80 mm: both found 100 %, paired right by charge 98 %, + profile 100 %, production gate 50 %; 80–400 mm: both found 100 %, paired right by charge 95 %, + profile 100 %, production gate 40 %. 30 single-donor controls reproduce production: 100 %.

Earlier work: wft/MULTITRACK_2026-09-14.md measured the same rule on the n_TOF run_145 overlay bench (beam seeder): swaps among time-coincident pairs 24 → 14 % (A) and 23 → 7 % (C) with pairing on. No Geant4 / Garfield study of the pairing exists; the response simulation (MX17_Geant) could make one.

11

Details

The y view is fitted and on M3; x has no candidate. A near-vertical x track puts its whole drift column on 1–2 strips, and det3 x shares little charge (kernel c1 = 0.05), so the ±1 neighbours sit at 7–9 % of the brightest strip: 15–50σ signals, but under the 10 % relative floor, which leaves 2 strips, one short of MIN_STRIPS = 3. 2 % of rays at |tan θx| < 0.01 and zero above 0.08.

Plain MIN_STRIPS = 2 recovers 17/17, but on 742 triggers whose M3 track misses det3 it adds 12 fits (edge noise bands, faint blips).

Head-on rule (reco_variant.py --headon-sig 20): MIN_STRIPS stays 3; a 2-strip cluster is admitted when its weaker strip is ≥ 20σ. Head-ons have it at 55–320σ, the fakes at ≤ 9σ. 17/17 detected, 400/400 controls detected (production 400), 0 control views moved; 0 fits added on the empty-chamber set.

12

Details

headon2.py. Signal: 845 x and 1107 y interior head-on rays (|tan| < 0.03, the other view fitted). The donor’s strips within ±4 mm of its M3 footprint are scaled by k and added onto a real noise plane of an event whose M3 track misses det3 and in which production finds nothing (x: 1128 of 1339); noise ×2 (n_TOF after 23 July) adds a second noise plane × √3 and takes hit significance against 2σ. Hits are emulated from the waveforms (significance = 1.3 · max / noise, threshold 5: matches mm_processor to r = 0.98–1.00). Found = a seed whose charge centroid is within 2 mm of M3. Fakes: the same noise planes with nothing added, with the t0 and charge (× k) of a random real track of the other view: the rule fires at all.

Rules stack on production (they act only when the plane has no seed): 2-strip ≥ 20σ (the rule of the previous slide); 1 strip ≥ 7σ; column finder: per strip, the charge integrated over the other view’s drift window [t0 − 120, t0 + 1020] ns against a baseline from outside it, Z ≥ 10, starting inside the window and lasting ≥ 6 samples. Charge-checked: the rescued cluster’s window charge must match the other view’s fitted charge, |ln(Q/(R·q_other))| ≤ 3σ, with R and σ from detected head-ons (x: R = 4.79, σ = 0.071) — the same x/y charge equality that pairs two tracks. Without it the 1-strip rule fires on 1.9–2.8 % of empty planes; with it ≤ 0.03 %.

End to end in wft (headon3.py: both views injected at gain k, hits emulated, wft seeding with WFT_HEADON_SIG = 20, the worker fit with WFT_HEADON_RESCUE): x|1|0.05: production 73 % → 83 % found, fakes 0.0 → 0.0 %; x|1|0.1: production 90 % → 93 % found, fakes 0.0 → 0.0 %; x|1|1: production 93 % → 98 % found, fakes 0.0 → 0.0 %; x|2|0.05: production 43 % → 67 % found, fakes 0.0 → 0.0 %; x|2|0.1: production 77 % → 90 % found, fakes 0.0 → 0.0 %; x|2|1: production 93 % → 98 % found, fakes 0.0 → 0.0 %; y|1|0.05: production 87 % → 87 % found, fakes 0.0 → 0.0 %; y|1|0.1: production 90 % → 90 % found, fakes 0.0 → 0.0 %; y|1|1: production 88 % → 88 % found, fakes 0.0 → 0.0 %; y|2|0.05: production 57 % → 63 % found, fakes 0.0 → 0.0 %; y|2|0.1: production 87 % → 87 % found, fakes 0.0 → 0.0 %; y|2|1: production 88 % → 88 % found, fakes 0.0 → 0.0 %.

y needs none of this at 490 V (its strips share more charge); at k ≤ 0.1 with doubled noise the same rules recover y too (headon2.json). Not covered: tracks that are head-on in BOTH views (no other view to lean on) and a busy plane (another particle), which is the multi-particle problem.

M3 reference

13

Details

Split of all 126 interior rays in the spark category (sparks.py), from the full-plane waveforms: discharge = a view with > 150 strips above SNR 6 or > 100 strips swinging below −10 σ (chip-wide ringing); muon+other = in both views the charge on the M3 footprint is a single, track-wide cluster and anything else sits > 5 mm away; shower = the rest (the cluster at the crossing is wide or branching). Checked by eye on random displays of each class.

What a discharge looks like here: the strips of whole DREAM chips (64 channels) jump together in the same samples — horizontal bands in the display — with saturated strips and a negative swing on hundreds of channels. In most examples the muon’s own trace is visible on M3 before the band, consistent with the earlier finding that det3 sparks are muon-induced (4× more likely with a track).

“muon+other” is mostly a clean track plus either a second particle far away or a slow baseline swing on a distant chip that crosses the 10 % floor (the floor is relative to the brightest strip, and a modest MIP makes it low). The 50-hit veto counts both planes together, so an inclined track (40+ strips in y) plus anything else trips it.

Recovery test: the production reconstruction (reco_variant.py --no-spark-veto, finalize environment) on all 126, scored with the budget’s rule (both views, r ≤ 5 mm, n_dropped ≤ 2). discharge: 2/32 detected as production would count it (r ≤ 5 mm AND n_dropped ≤ 2), 5 within 5 mm, chosen fit agreeing with M3 in both views in 4, some candidate agreeing in both views in 4; muon+other: 0/49 detected as production would count it (r ≤ 5 mm AND n_dropped ≤ 2), 20 within 5 mm, chosen fit agreeing with M3 in both views in 19, some candidate agreeing in both views in 34; shower: 4/45 detected as production would count it (r ≤ 5 mm AND n_dropped ≤ 2), 4 within 5 mm, chosen fit agreeing with M3 in both views in 0, some candidate agreeing in both views in 0. The chosen fits that agree carry n_dropped = 24–86 (muon+other): the other deposit is a competing cluster, so with the veto gone they would still fall to the n_dropped > 2 cut. Lifting the veto recovers them only together with the cut decision of the “found, cut” category; and like MULTI, 15 of the 49 have M3 only among the runners-up.

A better rule than a hit count: veto on the discharge signature itself (chip-wide simultaneous bands, the negative swing), and let the candidate fit handle busy-but-clean events.

δ-rays: a knock-on electron leaves its own track; the straight-line fit takes both

Rutherford knock-on rate vs what det3 shows · event 28537

DELTA class

controls

M3 reference

production fit

14

Details

Physically: the muon kicks an atomic electron hard. The rate of a knock-on above T falls as ξ/T (ξ ≈ 0.34 keV for 30 mm of argon at 1 atm), and its path length rises steeply with T: a 10 keV δ goes ~2 mm (a blob), a 30 keV one ~1 cm, a 50 keV one ~3 cm (CSDA path in argon, approximate: ESTAR water values scaled by the stopping-power ratio; the projected extent is shorter because the electron scatters). So about 1 % of crossings carry a δ long enough to widen the cluster by ≳ 8 mm — the classifier’s threshold — and the observed DELTA share is 0.93 %.

In the data: a wide cluster that grows sideways out of the track at one depth, often curling, often ending in a bright spot (where the electron stops and dE/dx peaks). The fit has one straight line and a non-negative charge profile along it, so it tilts to pass through the δ’s charge.

Recoverable? Partly, in principle: the muon’s part of the column is usually still straight and on M3. The two-track fit does not do it (it looks for a second straight line: any candidate agrees in 10 % of DELTA views with it on, vs 8 % in production). A robust fit that down-weights charge far from the line, or a track + free-form-blob model, could. Not tried here. The gas mixture of the June bench was not recorded; ξ uses pure argon, which the few-% quencher changes by a few %.

What the fit does with a saturated strip today: a fixed 3550 cut, one side only

15

Details

Code: wft/model.py. prep_plane builds the mask sat = W_raw ≥ SAT (SAT = the bundle’s sat_adc = 3550, on the pedestal + CM subtracted samples before the gain division; dead channels are added to the same mask). _solve_nnls drops masked samples from the weighted NNLS for the depth-charge profile, then adds Σ max(0, W − model)² / σ² over the masked samples: the model is pushed up to the clip but never pulled down. The χ² dof count excludes them. WFT_SAT_SOLVE=1 (opt-in, off in production) re-solves with the model held at the clip on samples where it falls below (a Tobit active set); FINDINGS §41 found it does not fix the 5–12 % charge deficit of saturated tracks, and that angle/position were unchanged by censoring on the bench resolution sample.

Nothing else knows about saturation: the rest of a clipped strip’s samples — the rising edge, the falling edge after the plateau and the undershoot — are fitted with the same linear, amplitude-independent electronics template as an unsaturated strip, and so are the neighbours’ copies through the sharing kernel. Next slide: what the rail actually looks like.

The rail is not at 3550, and the more strips sit on it, the more fits fail

det3 waveforms (1,324 events) · all golden-row fits, one-cluster views

x view

y view

16

Details

Left: the maximum of every strip above 3000 ADC in the satfit sample. The pile-up is the ADC rail, 4095 − pedestal − common mode: it sits at 3650–3900 and varies per channel and per sample, not at the bundle’s 3550. Within one clipped plateau the CM moves the clipped value by a median 72 ADC (90 %: 248); 1,729 of 44,697 samples inside a plateau (3.9 %) fall below 3550 and are fitted as exact measurements. Plateaus last a median 6 samples (360 ns).

The bottom rail. After the plateau, 58 % of clipped strips swing down to ADC 0: the strip’s max − min is 4100 ADC, the full 12-bit range (median undershoot -248 ADC; unsaturated bright strips undershoot by a median 2.1 % of their peak). Those bottom-clipped samples are fitted as data too. Whether the electronics are still linear there (a template undershoot of a 3–10× larger true pulse) or recovering from overload cannot be told from these strips alone.

Right: production fits, views with one hit cluster, by the number of saturated hits. Fraction disagreeing with M3 (|dθ| > 5° or |res| > 3 mm). 10 % (x) and 11 % (y) of views have ≥ 3 saturated strips. When a saturated fit fails, it reads too STEEP in 90 % (x) / 86 % (y) of cases (median |tan| excess 0.32 / 0.64); χ²/dof median: failed 2336, saturated-but-fine 438, unsaturated 40 (x).

Saturation is correlated with everything else that is bright (δ-rays, blobs, two particles), so the right panel is not by itself the effect of the censoring rule: the next two slides separate them.

What a failed saturated track looks like: a faint MIP line plus one compact, very bright blob

FIT_SAT examples: red boxes = censored samples, blue = bottom-rail samples fitted as data

the blob is a short δ-electron stopping: 5–20 keV in 1–5 mm, 1–3× the whole MIP track’s charge on 2–4 strips

M3 reference

production fit

sample ≥ 3550 (censored)

sample ≤ −200 on a clipped strip (fitted as data)

17

Details

Most FIT_SAT failures are not a saturated MIP column. The track itself is faint and on M3; the saturated strips belong to one compact deposit deep in the gap, often 1–4 mm off the line. A low-energy knock-on electron (δ) of 5–20 keV travels only 1–5 mm in argon, depositing as much charge as the whole MIP track (≈ 3 cm × ~2.5 keV/cm) on a few strips — so it saturates them. P(T > 5 keV) ≈ 7 %, P(T > 10 keV) ≈ 3 % per crossing (previous slide’s ξ/T), the same order as the 10 % of views with ≥ 3 saturated strips.

Why the fit fails: its model is one straight line with a non-negative charge profile along it. The blob holds most of the charge, so χ² is dominated by it and the line tilts to reach it (the "too steep" of the previous slide). The next slide tests whether the treatment of the clipped samples is to blame: it is not — even with every saturated strip removed the line still tilts, because the blob’s unsaturated edges and neighbours hold enough charge off the MIP line.

So the fix aimed at this failure is the model, not the mask: a straight track + one free compact deposit (position, time, charge, its own width), which would let the MIP part fix the line.

Even dropping every saturated strip leaves the agreement where it was: the blob’s unsaturated charge pulls the line.

18

Details

satfit.py: each saturated event (≥ 3 saturated hits in a view; 924 events) and 400 unsaturated controls, refitted with the production fitter (wft.reco.fit_plane, phys bundle, t0 prior, WFT_PIVOT_START=1, which reproduces the table to < 0.05 mm) on a rebuilt window (the SNR > 6 cluster under the production fit ± 3 strips). Only the censor mask changes between arms: low = censor ≥ 3300; both = ≥ 3300 and, on a strip that clipped, every sample ≤ −200 dropped; tail = everything after a strip’s first clipped sample; strip = every sample of a clipped strip. Numbers above the bars: views that start / stop agreeing with M3 against production.

Controls have no saturated sample, so only low/both can change them (the 3300 cut can catch a bright unsaturated sample).

Reading it: the failures are 91 % angle and 74 % position failures in production, and their |dθ| 90th percentile stays at ~31° under every rule. The rules do lower χ²/dof (the clipped and bottom-rail samples were badly modelled), but the line does not move: the blob’s rising edges and its unsaturated neighbours (through the sharing kernel) carry enough charge off the MIP line to tilt it on their own. Any rule in the set agrees in 77 % of views (vs 71 %), so per-event rule shopping would not help either.

What this does not test: an amplitude-dependent template, a per-channel rail from the pedestal file, or a track + blob model. The first two are about charge (FINDINGS §41), not geometry; the third is the one aimed at this failure.

“Clean, fit off” is mostly two close tracks the classifier could not separate

FIT class, 0.34 % of interior rays: no saturation, one cluster within 5 mm of M3

two tracks a few mm apart, or a V from one point: the fit lands between them

M3 reference

production fit

19

Details

The C22 classifier calls a view "clean" when nothing else sits more than 5 mm from the footprint and the cluster is not too wide. By eye most FIT events are two tracks within a few mm (parallel, or a V from a common vertex: a δ emitted forward, or a pair), plus some long-tailed single tracks. A single straight line goes between them.

Recoverable? This is the two-track fit’s regime, below its separation limit (notes/two-track-limit: the trigger fires on ~0 % of inclined pairs under 12 mm). With WFT_TWO_TRACK_FIT=1 any candidate agrees in 35 % vs 34 % without: no gain today. Small share.

The rest is the reference’s own error or the chamber edge

the remaining det3 interior categories

Position tail: 0.22 %

Right angle, one clean cluster, > 3 mm from M3. About ⅔ are muons that scattered between the M3 doublets (a kink a 4-layer χ² < 1 cannot see). The reference is wrong; nothing to recover.

Edge: 0.29 %

Interior by the budget’s rule but near the edge of the OTHER coordinate (< 8 mm) or the field distortion zone: a truncated or bent column. Geometry, not reconstruction.

20

Details

C22 report (notes/mx17-outliers-vs-m3) has the evidence for the bent-track fraction (kinkvtx.py: 0.65 ± 0.07 of the position tail) and the edge response.
